My parent is a marine biologist, and when they were younger, they spent time watching whales and seals out in the ocean for hours, hoping to see a stream of water many kilometers away. If you see one, it's fantastic because you can get so close to the whales that you can touch them. If you don't, which is very likely, you could spend days doing nothing while looking at the horizon, hoping. It was common to be out for about 8 hours at a time in small boats. These days, they say they stay in hotels; back then, they camped, which is okay for a while, but not for months.

They also stayed on deserted islands looking at seals for months, with a boat bringing water, cigarettes, and food every few days. It was really not fun when they smoked all the cigarettes before the boat came, which is why they quit. They and their friends had to collect the butts from the sand and try to make new ones. They said once they realized how miserable they were, shaking with anxiety while looking for butts in the cold night sand, they just couldn't smoke anymore. They also got bitten in the rear by a baby seal. Bathing was hard as there were a lot of sharks near the island, and they got really close to the shore, so you couldn't get very deep into the sea. Once, they were left alone in the sea swimming because a friend got scared and swam to the shore, with a lot of sharks around.

It's really boring to be alone on an island with no electricity for days. Also, the islands in that region are quite barren. The cancer risk is real; spending all that time under the sun can really affect you. A paleontologist that my other parent worked with had serious issues from sun exposure.

There are a lot of cool stories too; they saw orcas once, and people can try to find them for years, but they were lucky enough to find them in the wild. Their eyesight is also amazing; when on vacation, they grab drinks and stare into the horizon until they find dolphins, which usually doesn't take long. Since they are kind of easy to find, I'm pretty good at it too. They can also see a fin or a tail for half a second and know which whale they are looking at.

There are many stories about dolphins swimming by ships and hanging out with military personnel, riding on big military vessels—good times overall. My other parent once impressed a bunch of sailors with their fishing skills.

Overall, the job involves a lot of work and a lot of fun and amazing experiences, but the sad reality is that the pay is poor, and you can't settle down. Ultimately, my parent left to work in the pharmaceutical industry, and my other parent rejected a master's in geology to work and settle down. Even if they pursued their careers, it would have been impossible to start a family, and earning a lead research role is nearly impossible unless you are second in command when the lead dies.
